task: Analysis-use diagnosis of Q2 reconstruction, Q3 HRS longitudinal reconstruction, and earlier HAALSI prospective case
status: bounded audit complete; historical studies remain closed
method: Read local manuscript, tasks, source exports, actual candidate programs/specifications and complete aggregate results. No generator invocation/import, no synthetic cohort creation, no raw clinical table access, no frozen file changes, no new threshold, no web search. One separate deterministic HRS integration/calculation is recorded.

endpoints: E1: HbA1c~age+female+BMI, BMI term, percentage points/(kg/m^2)
E2: HbA1c~age+female+glucose, glucose term, percentage points/(mmol/L)
E3: HbA1c~female+BMI+glucose+age, age term, percentage points/year

boundary.source_inputs: Both arms received external evidence, population/measurement definitions and all analysis definitions. R additionally received all 30 existing CHNS reference summaries; L did not receive them in its scoped author inputs. Same reference case was previously exposed to project investigators. The statistical supplement also received all 30 summaries.
boundary.target_status: Observed linked complete-case CHNS 2009 sample, ages 35-74; developmental reference. No concealed statistic among the 30 in R or the statistical supplement.
boundary.feedback: Both phases permitted feedback; all six retained their laws after the additional stage. Initial/final deliveries duplicate, not revision gains. Source-context numerical replay unavailable.
boundary.count: One clinical case; six agent laws (3 L,3 R), 18 distinct 3000-row delivery tables. 36 initial/final delivery slots plus 6 trial outputs =42 successful executions and24 distinct tables. Separate statistical supplement adds one law/3 valid tables; three pre-start orchestration failures are retained.

direct: All3 reference slopes supplied to R and STAT_R30.
derived: R constructors used joint latent mixture laws and deterministic calibration to supplied observed-variable projections; statistical comparator uses covariance-based separate OLS projections.
assumed: Mixture class overlap, unreported covariate correlations and distributional forms; R02/R03 and statistical comparator assume sex independent.

analyses.supported_use: Reconstruct these three supplied adjusted projections jointly in one analyzable cohort; all three R laws and the statistical law produce close finite-sample values.
analyses.unsupported_use: Unseen conditional effects, individualized prediction, source/transport uncertainty, clinical precision, superiority to statistical calibration or added-revision benefit.

diagnosis.reason: The successful endpoints are explicit fitting information; all3 R means are near supplied coefficients. L uses incomplete external information and differs. This explains the evidential status without treating matching as learning an unreported relation.
diagnosis.alternatives: Design does not isolate information alone from authors’ model choices; only3 constructors/arm and one exposed case.

analyses.smallest_followup: No further sampling. Retain each endpoint’s adjustment set and label it supplied-summary reconstruction; use an actually withheld question only in a separately predeclared future evaluation if needed.

direct: Both reference correlations supplied to R and STAT_R30.
derived: Mixture dependence permits high Pearson but lower Spearman; R01/R03 use correlated broad/narrow components and STAT_R30 uses shared upper-rank regime.
assumed: Tail class identity/overlap and dependence within regimes are unreported.

analyses.supported_use: Demonstrates simultaneous reconstruction of two distinct supplied dependence statistics on the same paired measurements.
analyses.unsupported_use: Tail co-occurrence probabilities or subgroup correlations not supplied; agreement does not identify the complete copula.

diagnosis.reason: R Pearson means0.65056-0.66644 and Spearman0.35757-0.36098 approach supplied0.66097/0.36146; L Spearman0.50134-0.56648 is consistently higher. The statistical law also approximates both without recovering a unique joint distribution.
diagnosis.alternatives: Residual sampling variation and different mixture structures explain some finite-table discrepancy; causal contribution of any one modeling choice was not isolated.

analyses.smallest_followup: Report these two correlations separately; keep unsupplied tail analyses explicitly unassessed. No new component or closed-case tuning is warranted.

direct: All25 marginal mean/SD/quantile values supplied to R and STAT_R30.
derived: Lognormal/Bernoulli/discrete-age and mixture parameters reconstructed from allowed summaries; comparator uses bounded marginal calibration.
assumed: Support beyond quantiles, continuous density shape, mixture identification and parameter uncertainty.

analyses.supported_use: Approximate reproduction of supplied central distribution summaries in finite generated cohorts, with all25 diagnostics retained.
analyses.unsupported_use: Recovery of real extremes, rare-event risk, conditional distributions, subject-level realism or sample-design uncertainty.

diagnosis.reason: Fitting a finite list of moments/quantiles does not identify a distribution. Actual generators use different positive-support mixture or bounded laws even when means and SDs agree.
diagnosis.alternatives: Minor finite-sample mismatch may be ordinary sampling; no equivalence threshold or new pass rule is imposed.

analyses.smallest_followup: Keep complete diagnostics and tail assumptions alongside the available cohort. No further fitting of this closed exposed reference.

observed_result.retained_fit_verification: All6 valid fits returned16 terms and passed existing independent conditional-GLS coefficient/SE checks; not independent REML validation.

boundary.source_inputs: Both authors had published HRS demographic tables, fitted conditional models and all16 intended memory coefficients; no HRS individual records.
boundary.target_status: Same published-model reconstruction; coefficients and Table2 original/synthetic summaries were legitimate source inputs. Not held-out biological discovery.
boundary.count: One HRS example; two constructions; 3 fixed seeds each; 11509 synthetic subjects x4 balanced visits. Nine physical generations:3 agent+3 invalid initial comparator+3 valid corrected comparator. Only6 valid tables in comparison.
boundary.source_precision: Printed point estimates are rounded fitted sample estimates, fixed as plugin model parameters. Synthetic intervals are conditional on the generating model; parameter/source uncertainty and real attrition are not reconstructed.

direct: All16 memory fixed coefficients and source SEs; random intercept/slope/residual summaries; all sequential conditional model coefficients.
derived: Gamma shape=1/phi and scale=mu*phi; random effect covariance from variances or rounded SDs andrho.
assumed: Plugin coefficients fixed; independent innovations; Gaussian effects; static baseline HbA1c; balanced0,2,4,6 visits.

analyses.supported_use: Implement and refit the specified longitudinal mixed model, including both spline branches, interactions and correlated subject effects; below-knot negative direction preserved in6/6 valid tables.
analyses.unsupported_use: Stable sign/significance for the weak upper interaction, new population transport, causal glycemic effects, treatment/attrition dynamics or accuracy superiority.

diagnosis.reason: Both valid programs encode +0.012867 and the identical16-term mean law; evaluator matches source spline and factor coding. Upper source estimate/SE=0.997. Native standardized errors are-1.107,-0.878,-2.341; agent1.385,0.047,0.939. Five intervals contain source coefficient and five contain zero, with different exceptions. Sampling can plausibly give observed signs, but the aggregate check does not prove it is the sole cause.
diagnosis.alternatives: Real source-model misspecification and narrowed upper HbA1c range affect applicability/information. Three seeds cannot establish an accuracy ranking; one native estimate lies2.34 fitted SEs below source. The earlier parser bug is separate, repaired and excluded.

analyses.smallest_followup: Keep the original closed3-seed batch. Independent review of the new deterministic audit and source-to-parameter mapping is sufficient now; report conditional sampling limits and the separate original-distribution mismatch, not another generator or favorable-seed search.

analysis.endpoints: All27 baseline distribution/count fields; explicit below/above6.5 HbA1c subgroup moments.

direct: Original and paper-synthetic subgroup moments; published model coefficients/dispersion and demographic counts.
derived: Deterministic recursive-law integration gives upper HbA1c mean7.149615 andSD0.560018, lowerSD0.649547; all use existing specification without sampling.
assumed: Gamma conditional HbA1c family, uniform ages within bins including80-100, recursive independence.

analyses.supported_use: Reproduce the published simulation law’s distribution, and demonstrate transparently where that law differs from the original sample summaries.
analyses.unsupported_use: Accurate original-cohort high-HbA1c dispersion, tail-risk analysis, empirical distribution equivalence or automatic repair of a scientific source-model limitation.

diagnosis.reason: The deterministic law already implies upperSD~0.56, far from printed original1.4 and close to paper synthetic0.6. The discrepancy persists without finite sampling; both implementations inherit it. LowerSD~0.65 also exceeds original0.4. It is not an implementation sign error, and the original empirical values are rounded sample estimates rather than exact constraints.
diagnosis.alternatives: The original model was fitted with limited conditional form; measurement mixture, tail heterogeneity or higher-order misspecification may contribute, but their causal roles are untested.

analyses.smallest_followup: Accept the model-reconstruction use with explicit original-distribution limits. If upper-tail analysis becomes the actual intended use, first obtain adequate source tail/conditional summaries and test their compatibility; do not alter the closed benchmark to match now-visible values.

analysis.definition: Glucose contrast per5kg/m^2 BMI, adjusting age and recorded sex
analysis.outcome: released cleaned capillary point-of-care glucose, mmol/L

observed_result.historical_primary_rule: All3 endpoints x3 seeds <=0.10; at least4/5 agent laws per case. HAALSI3/5; S01 fails. WaveA expansion stopped. Thresholds0.05/0.10/0.20/0.30 gave1/3/5/5 agent laws. Zero effects satisfy all3 HAALSI margins. No new cutoff introduced.

boundary.source_inputs: Target age eligibility and pooled capillary point-of-care measurement definition; MIND-China fasting-serum marginal means/SDs and Ayele age/sex/BMI margins. Ayele adjusted binary diabetes ORs remained contextual, not continuous-glucose slopes. No numeric HAALSI target moments or coefficients supplied.
boundary.target_status: Prospectively withheld exact HAALSI estimates, revealed after all constructors closed. Unweighted complete-case finite-sample projections among4394 eligible records, age>=40, no fasting requirement; not population or causal estimands.
boundary.count: One case with5 independent agent laws and1 prescribed law;3 seeds each,5000 rows/table. Initial/final slots are retained aliases. No new sampling or reopening is performed in this audit.
boundary.source_limit: Strict source replay unavailable for unspecified weights/divisors; approximate marginal comparisons cannot identify the required conditional dependence or transport between fasting serum and pooled capillary measurements.

direct: Source glucose/BMI/age margins and covariate categories; no target continuous-glucose conditional coefficient or sex-specific slope supplied.
derived: Moment-to-lognormal/beta transformations; count ratios; recorded glucose under each assumed feeding/device model.
assumed: All age/BMI glucose loadings, sex modification, target composition and source-to-target measurement transport. S01 explicitly uses independent glucose, so its population projection coefficients are zero.

analyses.supported_use: Bounded empirical preservation of positive descriptive direction for this finite HAALSI sample under all5 constructed laws.
analyses.unsupported_use: Quantitatively reliable association strength, nonzero-signal recovery established by the pass rule, causal effects, reliable arbitrary downstream use or broad transport.

diagnosis.reason: All15 agent draws preserve the positive direction, but loadings are assumed: glucose age factors0.10-0.20 and positive BMI loadings were built into the candidate copulas. They do not follow uniquely from marginal means/SDs or adjusted binary-diabetes ORs. Magnitudes vary across laws; zero effects also pass the historical resolution.
diagnosis.alternatives: Feeding mixture, measurement scale, target demographic composition and omitted nonlinear dependence can also change projections. Existing data do not isolate these causal contributions.

analyses.smallest_followup: Retain the observed directional result separately from the failed case gate. If quantitative use is required elsewhere, obtain compatible adjusted continuous-glucose relationship evidence and predeclare an analysis-specific useful tolerance before evaluating new data; do not expand or tune this closed wave.

analyses.supported_use: Shows that interaction inference changes materially across admissible-looking complete-cohort constructions; identifies the unsupported effect-modification assumption.
analyses.unsupported_use: Reliable sign or magnitude of sex-specific BMI-glucose differences; sex-specific intervention or population inference.

diagnosis.reason: A01/A02 use smaller female BMI residual loadings(.26 vs.32; .22 vs.34), whereas A03/A04 use larger ones(.36 vs.27; .40 vs.30). The latter reverse the observed negative interaction on all3 seeds. A05 uses more complex sex/age/BMI dependence and has1 positive/2 negative estimates. These are explicit unreported assumptions, not a failure to reproduce an available sex-specific slope.
diagnosis.alternatives: Feeding mixture, measurement scale, target demographic composition and omitted nonlinear dependence can also change projections. Existing data do not isolate these causal contributions.

analyses.smallest_followup: For a future use, seek sex-stratified continuous glucose-BMI covariance/slopes with the same age adjustment and compatible capillary/feeding definition. Until then present interaction outputs as scenarios. Keep HAALSI closed; no fitting to revealed interaction.

actual_checks: Verified path existence and computed SHA256 of every provenance artifact listed.
Static inspection of every final Q2 agent generator, statistical comparator generator, both valid HRS generators/evaluator, and HAALSI model dependency code and parameters.
Read actual HRS published coefficient export and original R source definitions, with separate repaired-comparator accounting.
Recomputed source-to-fit standardized deviations for all96 HRS coefficients from retained aggregates; no fits rerun.
Derived HRS HbA1c truncated moments by quadrature and analytic Gamma moments at3 orders without RNG or individual rows.
Included all6 Q2 constructors, statistical supplement, all16 HRS coefficients/all27 diagnostics, all6 HAALSI constructors/all3 endpoints/all3 seeds.
Kept all original stopping rules and positive/negative results; initial/final aliases not counted as separate cohorts.
unresolved: HRS aggregate/static evidence does not prove sampling is the sole explanation of upper-branch sign difference.
HAALSI existing study does not causally separate missing conditional evidence, transport assumptions, measurement mixtures and generator-family choices.
No source or clinical validity is inferred from numerical checks alone.
